newsitem.title: JORDAN: Hamas condemns Israel-PLO deal on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Hamas condemns Israel-PLO deal on Hebron.

text.p: A spokesman for the Islamic militant group Hamas condemned on Friday an imminent Israeli-PLO accord on the West Bank town on Hebron and urged Palestinians to oppose peace with Israel.

"Hamas movement calls on the Palestinian people generally and the herioc people of Hebron in particular to reject and resist such plots," Ibrahim Ghosheh, an official spokesman for Hamas in Jordan, told Reuters.

"Sellout agreements that gave up rights on the land of Palestine are not binding to the youngest Palestinian child... Hamas vows that the path of Jihad (Islamic holy war) and legitimate resistance will remain open against the Zionist occupation," Ghosheh said.

Hamas leaders in Gaza have publicly said they would not use violence to oppose the self-rule deal between the Palestinian Authority and Israel. The Hamas leadership in Palestinian-ruled areas and abroad are believed to be divided over the issue of violence.

Israeli and Palestinian negotiating teams pressed ahead in late-night meetings on Thursday with drafting the text of a deal under which Israel would hand over 80 percent of Hebron, home to 400 Jews and 100,000 Arabs, to Palestinian self-rule.
Hamas was subjected to tough Israeli and PLO crackdowns after it carried out four suicide bombings in Israel in February and March that killed 59 people.

Ghosheh said the nearly concluded Hebron accord was an extension of the 1993 Israeli-PLO self-rule deal negotiated in the Norwegian capital Oslo that "has brought the Palestinians only humiliation and loss of land and rights."

"The danger of this (Hebron) accord is that it gives legitimacy to the partition of Hebron between Moslem Arabs and Jews and lays the basis for the Jewish quarter in Hebron with future agreement on expanding it," he said.
"The accord also more dangerously paves the way for the Judaisation of Jerusalem, legalising the Jewish settlements and full seizure of Palestine," Ghosheh added.
